title: Constructible cyclic module sheaves from finite abelian charts
statement: Let S be a scheme, n a nonzero natural number, and M a sheaf of modules over the lifted ring Z/n on S_et. If its underlying abelian sheaf is isomorphic to an abelian sheaf A admitting finite constant abelian charts on a finite constructible locally closed stratification, then M is constructible with finite module charts. Direct images, geometric stalks and the finite-module constructibility convention are [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] and [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. The assertion includes n = 1 and empty strata.

proof.text:
use the same finite stratification. Inverse image commutes with forgetting
coefficients, so its module restriction has the indicated underlying abelian sheaf.
The given finite constant charts provide a locally constant datum. Lift any geometric
point through their etale cover; the pullback-stalk and constant-stalk comparisons
identify its stalk with the finite abelian chart value. Transport through the given
abelian isomorphism. The finite-local-cyclic-module comparison now lifts these finite
abelian local systems to finite module charts. This comparison discards empty charts,
so neither empty schemes nor arbitrarily large constant values on empty charts cause
an exception. The argument works for every nonzero modulus, including modulus one.
